I like the idea on paper but I'd also have concerns about it being abused, like what if the moderator is also a bad actor? Especially with the ghost recordings, being able to record someone without their knowledge.

I'm sure there'll be an approval process for these powers, but bad actors can and will find ways around it. I'd like to suggest that all submitted evidence include a method of telling who recorded it, so that those who abuse the system can be found out and reported. Evidence is also sent directly to VRchat and not stored on the end user's machine. Even then I'd have concerns over screen recording using OBS. Moderators also only go where they're requested and can't hop around freely, with no way for instances to request a specific moderator (e.g. malicious instance host requesting a specific moderator so that moderator can record people in ghost mode without their knowledge).

Ericbazinga Thanks so much for the thoughtful feedback — I really appreciate it. Your concerns are completely valid, and I agree that any system involving stealth tools like Ghost Mode needs serious safeguards to prevent misuse or abuse by bad actors.

Here’s how the proposal addresses those exact concerns:

🔐 Accountability Built-In

Every clip, screenshot, and report automatically tags the moderator’s ID and cannot be edited or removed. This ensures transparency in every investigation.

Evidence is never stored locally — everything goes directly to VRChat’s servers for review, preventing hoarding or unauthorized sharing.

A backend audit trail logs all ghost joins and recording activity, so nothing happens off-record. Even if the users don’t see a ghost mod, staff can always verify actions after the fact.

🎯 No Free Roam – Demand-Only Access

VRCMs cannot jump between worlds at will. They can only enter:

Instances with staff approval,

Or flagged by automated community alert triggers (e.g., multiple active reports).

This prevents “ghost hopping” or targeting personal enemies.

🚫 No Host-Picked Mods

Users cannot request a specific moderator to join their instance.

The system auto-assigns VRCMs anonymously, so collusion isn’t possible between a host and a corrupt moderator.

🧪 Reviewable & Revocable

All VRCMs are held to strict rules:

Trial period + behavior audits

Monthly case reviews

Instant suspension if abuse is detected

Moderators who violate trust can be reported, reviewed, and removed.

✅ Big Picture

You're absolutely right — without restrictions, a system like this could be abused. But with the safeguards proposed (server-side evidence, identity tagging, controlled access, and oversight), it becomes a secure way to protect users while preventing unchecked power.

And of course, I’m always open to more ideas to strengthen it further. The goal is to support VRChat’s safety without ever compromising its freedom or trust.

Thanks again for voicing your concerns. It helps shape the proposal into something truly community-safe.

Yeah, I totally agree! I was gonna say the same thing. It's totally valid to worry about power abuse, and, like, paid staff and game devs have done it too. So, VR Chat could just boot anyone abusing it. The cool thing is, it doesn't cost VR Chat a monthly fee, and it makes things faster. If volunteers could use basic mod tools, like kicking people, it'd get rid of the problem for a bit. My idea was to give them the same tools the trust and safety team uses, so we can keep users safe quicker and take some pressure off the team. Plus, it'll get those YouTubers off their backs and keep the government away too.

Dear VRChat Team,

My name is Tyler (VRChat Username: Tyler.315275), and I’d like to formally propose a Volunteer Moderator Program (VRCM) for VRChat. This initiative would allow trained, vetted users to assist in observing and reporting TOS violations in public and semi-private worlds. The system prioritizes user safety, moderator protection, and staff collaboration—without giving volunteers ban powers or backend access.

---

🔧 Feature Summary

1. Ghost Observation Mode

Allows VRCMs to join instances invisible: not on player list, no mirror/avatar, no join pop-up, voice hidden.

Ideal for monitoring harassment, exploitation, or coordinated attacks.

2. Anonymous Display Name

Shows as “AnonymousObserver###” or hides nameplate entirely.

Prevents known violators from targeting or avoiding VRCMs.

3. Silent World Access

Shadow join into Public, Friends+, or Invite+ instances (staff approved).

Prevents bad actors from hiding in smaller rooms.

4. Community-Triggered Alerts

If 3+ users report someone in a short window, the system auto-pings a nearby VRCM to investigate in ghost mode.

5. Evidence Capture Tools

In-VR & desktop UI with:

Clip recording (timestamped, instance data)

Screenshot capture

Voice log (optional transcript)

Username tagging + annotations

One-click report submission to staff

6. Noclip/Freecam (Optional)

Investigation-only. VRCMs can move through geometry to observe exploiters.

Deactivated outside of active cases.

7. Training Program

Phase 1: Trial VRCM – shadow staff, no powers

Phase 2: Full VRCM – tools enabled, reviewed monthly

Optional promotion pipeline to Trust & Safety Team

---

🖥️ UI Mockup Attached

Attached is a basic 2D mockup of the VRCM user interface. The design is minimal and immersive, usable in VR or desktop mode. Core UI features include:

Ghost Mode toggle

Badge visibility toggle

Mic mute button

Clip/Screenshot/Tag/Submit evidence

Investigation console (report tracking, notes, status updates)

Pop-up alerts for community report triggers

Settings/help access

The mockup demonstrates how the system could integrate into the VRChat experience without disrupting gameplay or immersion.

---

✅ Benefits

Extends moderation coverage across time zones and events

Protects VRCMs from harassment via stealth tools

Improves report quality through timestamped, auto-tagged evidence

Strengthens trust and safety without granting punitive powers to non-staff

Creates a pipeline for identifying future Trust & Safety team members

---

Thank you for taking the time to review this proposal. I’d love to assist further—whether that’s designing expanded UI flows, documenting features, or helping test the system. I believe this could greatly enhance safety, accountability, and user trust within VRChat.

Warm regards,

Tyler
